examples.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ with real coefficients has roots $z_1=3+\textrm{i}$ and $z_2=3-\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $f(z).$
examples.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}z_1=3+\textrm{i}}$ and ${\color{black}z_2=3-\textrm{i}},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is ${\color{black}a=2},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =2(z-(3+\text{i}))(z-(3-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(z-(3+\text{i}))(z-(3-\text{i})) & =2({z}^{2}-(3+\text{i})z-(3-\text{i})z+(3+\text{i})(3-\text{i})) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-(3+\text{i}+3-\text{i})z+({3}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-6z+(9+1)) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-6z+10) \\  & =2{z}^{2}-12z+20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z) = 2z^2-12z+20.$

feedback.problem:
The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=16.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=16,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =16{(x-(-4))}^{2} \\  & =16(x+4)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}16(x+4)^{2} & =16({x}^{2}+8x+16) \\  & =16{x}^{2}+128x+256.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=16{x}^{2}+128x+256.$
